title: Quiz generator guardrails
description: Enforceable rules the builder validates a generated quiz against. severity=error blocks the emit; severity=warn surfaces a caution the merchant can override. Mirrors master Part 7 section 5.

rules.rule: Scored questions should be within the template's length band; hard-warn past ~8-10 unless category is formulation/subscription. Map length to category, do not globally minimize.
Easy/concrete questions first; demographics/personal/email late; never two high-effort questions (ranking, long multi-select) back to back.
No double-barreled, leading, or loaded question. One concept per question; neutral wording describing the shopper's need, not the product's virtues.
Answer options are mutually exclusive and collectively exhaustive; numeric ranges must not overlap; include an Other/None/Not-sure escape when the set cannot be exhaustive.
Single-select <=7 options as radios/cards (ideal <=5); 8+ options must render as a dropdown.
Never emit a slider. Scale questions render as 3-5 discrete labeled tap points.

Multi-select only with a capped list (~5-6) and normalized scoring (score by proportion of matched attributes, not raw count) so selecting more boxes cannot auto-win. Prefer forced-choice yes/no per item for short lists.
Randomize nominal option order across respondents (pin Other/Not-sure last, exempt); keep ordinal scales in logical order. Randomize display only, never the outcome.
Every question must change at least one filter or score for at least one product. A question whose answers never alter any outcome is removed/flagged.
Every branch is reachable and every path terminates at a result. No unreachable or non-terminating paths.

Every reachable result path resolves to >=1 product, validated against the live catalog, with an empty-set fallback ladder defined (relax least-important filter -> weighted closest-match -> best-seller). The single most important runtime guardrail.
Same answers must always yield the same recommendation. Scoring is a pure function of (answers, catalog snapshot); no randomness, time, or inventory-order dependence in outcomes.
A deterministic tie-break chain is defined: primary-question weight -> priority/popularity attribute -> stable sort by product id.
No single question can dominate scoring: cap per-question contribution; normalize multi-select.
Attribute vocabulary is small and shared across products, reusing catalog tags/metafields (Shopify Search & Discovery filters/synonyms) rather than free-form.
A 'because you chose X and Y' rationale is generable from the specific answers that drove the match/score.

Place the email gate late - after the shopper has invested answers, at/just before the result - never the first screen. Category-dependent: at_result for diagnostic/formulation/pack/pet/shade; deferred_to_action for fit/durables/gifting.
Native, labeled controls: real input type=radio/checkbox, one label per option; radio groups announce as a group and are arrow-navigable. No div-with-click-handler controls.
Every option, including image tiles, has a text label; images are not the only signal.
Sufficient color contrast (AA), selection state not conveyed by color alone, mobile-first hit targets >=24px.
rules.source: WCAG 2.5.8; enforced on inherited brand palette
